title: Perfectionism (Adaptive vs. Maladaptive)
description: A personality style characterized by striving for flawlessness and setting excessively high standards. Adaptive perfectionism fuels excellence; maladaptive perfectionism fuels self‑criticism and fear of failure.
shortDescription: A personality style characterized by striving for flawlessness and setting excessively high standards. Adaptive perfectionism fuels excellence; maladaptive perfectionism fuels self‑criticism and fear of failure.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: A personality style characterized by striving for flawlessness and setting excessively high standards. Adaptive perfectionism fuels excellence; maladaptive perfectionism fuels self‑criticism and fear of failure.

sections.title: Core Characteristics
content: Adaptive: high standards, but accepts mistakes as part of growth, flexible.
Maladaptive: unrealistically high standards, harsh self‑criticism, all‑or‑nothing thinking, procrastination due to fear of imperfection.

sections.title: Behavioral Patterns
content: Adaptive: works hard, meets deadlines, feels satisfied after achievement.
Maladaptive: rewrites emails 10 times, misses deadlines because “it’s not ready,” avoids tasks where they might fail.

sections.title: Communication Style
content: Adaptive: “I want to do this well.”
Maladaptive: “If it’s not perfect, it’s worthless.”

sections.title: Strengths
content: Maladaptive: none—it undermines the very excellence it seeks.

sections.title: Weaknesses
sections.content: Maladaptive: burnout, anxiety, depression, relationship strain from impossible standards.

sections.title: Decision-Making Style
content: Maladaptive: paralyzed by choice, over‑researches, never satisfied with any option.
Adaptive: sets criteria, decides, moves on.

sections.title: Relationship Patterns
sections.content: Maladaptive perfectionists often expect perfection from partners, leading to criticism and dissatisfaction.

sections.title: Workplace Behavior
content: Maladaptive: stuck in details, misses deadlines, frustrates colleagues.

sections.title: Leadership Style
content: Adaptive perfectionist leaders set high but achievable standards.
Maladaptive perfectionist leaders are micromanagers who demoralize teams.

sections.title: Stress Response
sections.content: Stress is heightened because any error is a catastrophe.

sections.title: How to Identify It
content: Ask: “When was the last time you turned in work that was ‘good enough’?”
Look for intense frustration over minor mistakes.

sections.title: Common Misconceptions
content: Perfectionism isn’t the same as striving for excellence. The healthy version forgives; the unhealthy version punishes.
It’s not a “humble brag”; it’s often a deeply painful trap.

sections.title: Real-World Scenario
sections.content: A designer with maladaptive perfectionism spends 40 hours on a draft. Her colleagues produce acceptable work in 10. She’s praised for quality but eventually let go because she can’t meet deadlines. Her need to be perfect made her professionally unviable.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: Perfectionism is a shield against criticism. But the shield is so heavy you can’t move. Let “good enough” be a victory, not a defeat.
